A ~8 cm arm (62009 + 62004, d 0-5.8, ~24k) leaves the stop vertex at a clear kink, near-perpendicular in the c and e azimuths; 155008 (1.2 cm compact, 6.5-7.2 cm out) sits right at the far end of that arm in e, so I read it as the arm end rather than a detached dot. evidence: Chain is 56 cm but almost none of it is real track. Entry end at x=-314 (25.7 cm above the bottom anode, 6 cm from the z=298 face), fit end at x=-272 (67.5 cm from the bottom anode, 10 cm from the z face, 68 cm from the y=0 seam), bottom volume; dx=+42 of a 44 cm chord, so the fit end is the UPPER end (rule 7). All the real charge sits in a ~20 cm knot near the entry: 19007 (19.8 cm, 9.5e3 mean, ragged 1e4-6e4), 19009, delta 19008, and two shower-typed pieces 19005/19010, branching in several directions from a common region in the 3-D azimuths. No coherent spine, no plateau to read a Bragg rise against. Hard part: in f_meas a long grey track seems to run into the knot from higher time slices in W and V (and possibly U), so this knot may be the end region of a muon clustered elsewhere, but I cannot establish that from this cluster; judged as a broken blob with a fake spine.
